newsitem.title: USA: GM says Ohio strikers have returned to work.
newsitem.headline: GM says Ohio strikers have returned to work.

text.p: General Motors Corp said Wednesday that some 4,100 workers returned to work Wednesday morning at its Moraine, Ohio, sport utility vehicle assembly plant after a three-day strike.

Members of Local 801 of the International Union of Electronic Workers returned to the plant for their regular 0518 EST/1018 GMT shift, spokesman Tom Beaman of GM's truck group headquarters in Pontiac, Mich., said in a telephone interview.
As reported, a tentative agreement was reached Tuesday for the plant, near Dayton, which assembles the Chevrolet Blazer, GMC Jimmy and Oldsmobile Bravada sport utility vehicles.
Details were not disclosed. The plant lost two full days' production, or about 2,000 vehicles, GM said earlier.
